rationale: C12 supplies a concrete, material template for the child: the same Title 17 reciprocity proclamation machinery, the same sequence of statutory quotations and official-assurances finding, the same declaration that the foreign country's nationals receive Title 17 benefits, and a particularly close mechanical-reproduction proviso. C21 and C06 are also strong members of the same drafting family, but C12 most closely matches the child's operative limitation by applying section 1(e) only to compositions published after the proclamation's effective date and not previously mechanically reproduced in the United States.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas section 9 of the said title 17 provides in part that the copyright secured by such title shall extend to the work of an author or proprietor who is a citizen or subject of a foreign state or nation; (b) When the foreign state or nation...grants...to citizens of the United States the benefit of copyright on substantially the same basis as to its own citizens...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas section 9 of title 17...provides in part that the copyright secured by said title shall extend to the work of an author or proprietor who is a citizen or subject of a foreign state or nation only... '(b) When the foreign state or nation...grants...to citizens of the United States the benefit of copyright on substantially the same basis as to its own citizens...'
shared_material.explanation: The child reproduces the same statutory reciprocity foundation used in C12.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas satisfactory official assurances have been received that...citizens of the United States of America are entitled to obtain copyright in the United States of Brazil for their works on substantially the same basis as citizens of the United States of Brazil, including rights similar to those provided by section 1 (e)...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas a Sovereign Ordinance has been issued...whereby citizens of the United States as of this day are entitled to obtain copyright protection in the Principality of Monaco for all their artistic and literary works on substantially the same basis as nationals of Monaco, including rights similar to those provided by section 1(e)...
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same country-specific reciprocity finding and expressly include section 1(e) rights.

shared_material.child_excerpt: That there exist with respect to the United States of Brazil the reciprocal conditions specified in sections 1 (e) and 9 (b)...and that citizens of the United States of Brazil are entitled to all the benefits of the said title 17
shared_material.parent_excerpt: That as of this day the conditions specified in section (b) and 1(e) of title 17...exist and are fulfilled with respect to nationals of the Principality of Monaco, and that nationals...are entitled to all the benefits of the said title 17
shared_material.explanation: The operative declaration has substantially the same structure and legal effect, adapted to Brazil.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Provided, that the provisions of section 1 (e)...shall apply only to compositions published and copyrighted after the date of this proclamation which have not been reproduced in the United States prior to the date hereof on any contrivance by means of which the work may be mechanically performed.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: And provided further, that the provision of section 1(e)...shall apply only to compositions published on or after [this] day, and registered for copyright in the United States which have not been reproduced within the United States prior to this day on any contrivance by means of which the work may be mechanically performed.
shared_material.explanation: This distinctive, detailed proviso is an especially strong indication of direct reuse, with only timing and registration language adjusted.
